The THREE supplied images are the ONLY visual STYLE references, for solid matte #07080B silhouettes, hard 2D ink, stark flat slate shadow masses and restrained practical rim-light. The hood-up passenger in dark windbreaker, dark cargo trousers and rubber-soled shoes is a solid black ink silhouette with zero facial features. The nonhuman entity is also solid black with two subtle pale pinpoint eye glints, ONE head and FOUR long arms ending in FOUR hands. Cohesive hand-inked 2D for walls and objects. Single moment, no insets or extra foreground character; no text or watermark. No falling rain, mist, splash, flash, lightning, camera roll, shake or motion lines; static shallow deck puddles are okay.

Exact location anchor: An outdoor, three-metre-wide exterior passenger corridor on Deck 6 of a cruise ship at night. Viewed lengthwise along the corridor, the ship's dull off-white steel inner bulkhead with closed round portholes and a closed horizontal sliding cabin door is on the left; a thick rusty storm chain and padlock secure that door from the exterior. A row of orange life jackets hangs on individual wall hooks beside the door. On the right is a chest-high dark steel safety railing above the open black sea. An orange-dark rescue lifeboat hangs overhead from a steel davit, with its cable leading to a manual brake lever and separate locking bar stored on a bracket near the davit base. The steel deck is textured tread plate with shallow static puddles. Cool slate/cyan ship light and restrained warm sodium practical light illuminate the scene. The deck and props use a single cohesive hand-inked 2D graphic-noir medium. The sea and sky are outdoors. No painted falling rain, sea mist, lightning, flash, camera shake, rolling, motion trails, title or text overlay; transient effects are supplied later in Remotion.

P23 AFTERMATH, intentional state change: level-deck oblique view along the established 3m-wide corridor, with the long inner bulkhead running from near LEFT foreground toward the center distance, and the railing and open sea consistently on RIGHT. Do NOT add any wall across the far end of the corridor. On the left in the foreground the sole hooded survivor sits on the deck, back against the INNER bulkhead, both feet grounded, looking toward the faint dawn beyond the right-side railing. Behind them, the orange lifeboat has swung inward from its davit on the right and is held firmly against the SAME LEFT INNER SIDE WALL at adult torso height, visibly sandwiching one single black nonhuman shape. Its one head and four distinct hands remain visible above or to the side of the hull; no extra person and no gore. The single lifeboat cable can be followed from the hull upward over the davit pulley to its deck-mounted winch on the right; a solid locking pin is already inserted transversely through an off-center hole in the wheel's RIM AND its stationary bracket. Show one and only one locking pin, NOT a second rod in its storage bracket. Keep wheel, pin, cable and boat clearly separated and readable. Cool slate-blue, subtle sodium edge light and faint muted dawn, ink texture, still frame.
